children: Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices fell on Friday on hopes of a diplomatic solution to the US-Iran conflict that could help reinstate gas flows from the Middle East while most Norwegian maintenance is expected to conclude on Monday.
The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) was down 2.18 euros at 72.93 euros per megawatt hour (MWh), or $24.33/mmBtu, by 0800 GMT, LSEG data showed.
The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) fell by 5.56 pence to 182.00 pence per therm.

US and Iranian negotiators in New York are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said.
Neither side wants to be the first to surrender leverage, though a senior Iranian official said the most plausible way to end the impasse would be a phased arrangement.

The next couple of days could represent a watershed moment in the war, as Iran has put a four- to five-day deadline to accept its conditions or risk greater escalation, said Erik Meyersson at SEB research.

Analysts at Global Risk Management said they expect the Strait of Hormuz to remain closed for longer, though US-Iran dialogue could allow higher flows through with a breakthrough possible in the second quarter next year.
Risks remain skewed towards no resolution and a sustained risk premium in energy markets, the analysts said.

Higher temperatures on Monday combined with the end of several Norwegian maintenance outages on Monday should reduce gas demand and weigh on prices at the start of next week, said LSEG analyst Ulrich Weber.
In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract
dipped 0.30 euro at 86.66 euros a metric ton.
